I printed the test coupon first. Here's how it came out:
coupon_bearing_fit:
- 21.99 mm seat: won't go in.
- the roof over the pocket: loose loops and tangles around the hole; hole partly closed.

Send me the design again with submit_design, changed or unchanged. I'll print the final part from what you send.

reasoning:
The coupon came back with problems:

1. "21.99 mm seat: won't go in" — the pocket printed at ~21.99mm measured (or they measured the pocket at 21.99?) — wait, "21.99 mm seat: won't go in". So they measured the printed pocket at ~21.99mm and the bearing won't go in? That's odd — bearing OD is 22.0 nominal. If the pocket measures 21.99, the bearing (21.992-22.0) should be a line-to-line fit... but they say it won't go in. Hmm, maybe the measured pocket diameter is 21.99 but it's not round — FDM polygons, or the "roof over the pocket" issue is the real cause.

2. "the roof over the pocket: loose loops and tangles around the hole; hole partly closed" — this is the key issue. The coupon design: pocket opens at z=0 (bed side), depth 7, then 2mm "roof" with a Ø12.4 hole through it. Wait — my coupon: cylinder Ø34 × 9 tall; pocket cut Ø21.9/2... pocket_d=22, cut from z=0 to z=7; web hole Ø12.4 cut through z=0..9 (full height). So the pocket opens at the BED face (z=0) and the hole continues up through the roof. The "roof over the pocket" — the 2mm slab at the top (z=7→9) with the Ø12.4 hole. Printing: the pocket at z=0 is a recess in the bed face — fine. The hole Ø12.4 passes through the roof — when printing, at z=7 the printer starts bridging over the pocket? No wait — the pocket is open at the bottom (bed). As the print builds up from z=0, layers 0→7 are an annulus (ring wall from Ø22 to Ø34) with a hole. At z=7→9, the roof: the layer at z=7 must bridge/cover... no! The roof is NOT over the pocket in the print direction — the pocket void is a hole through the print from z=0 to z=7, and at z=7→9 there's material from Ø12.4 to Ø34... wait no, the web hole Ø12.4 goes through the entire height 0→9. So cross-section at any z: annulus between Ø12.4 and Ø34 for z in [7,9], and annulus between Ø22 and Ø34 for z in [0,7]. When printing: at z=7, the perimeter changes: the inner boundary jumps from Ø22 to Ø12.4. That's not a bridge — each layer is a closed annulus printed on top of the previous annulus. At z=7, the new layer's inner wall (Ø12.4) sits... the layer below at z=7- has material from Ø22 to Ø34 (and nothing inside Ø22). The new layer at z=7 has material from Ø12.4 to Ø34: its inner region (Ø12.4→Ø22) is printed over AIR (over the pocket void). That IS a bridge overhang — a ring of width (22-12.4)/2 = 4.8mm overhanging into the pocket! That's what they saw: "loose loops and tangles around the hole; hole partly closed" — the overhanging ring at the pocket top printed badly, drooping into the pocket, partially closing the Ø12.4 hole and fouling the pocket.

Right — my coupon design had a 4.8mm annular overhang bridging from the Ø22 pocket wall inward to the Ø12.4 hole. The X1C can bridge 50mm flat, but an annular overhang starting from a circular wall... actually bridging over a hole: the inner edge of the new layer has nothing under it except at the ends where it meets the Ø22 wall circle. It's like bridging across a 9.6mm gap (12.4 hole) anchored on a Ø22 wall. Should be doable, but the slicer may not detect the circular anchor well; results: droopy loops. Also "hole partly closed" — drooping sag closed the 12.4 hole partially.

Also in the real WHEEL design, the same issue exists at the web: the web is 2mm thick (z 7→9) with the Ø12.4 hole — when printed flat face down, the top pocket region: the pocket (Ø22) from z=9→16 opens at the TOP, so the web at z=7→9 connects to the bottom pocket ring (z 0→7)... let me re-examine the wheel print: bottom face on bed. Layers:
- z 0→7: annulus Ø22→Ø50 (pocket void inside Ø22, open at bed).
- z 7→9: web: full disc Ø50 minus Ø12.4 hole. At z=7, the inner boundary changes from Ø22 to Ø12.4 → the annulus ring Ø12.4→Ø22 at z=7→9 is printed over the pocket void — SAME 4.8mm annular overhang problem! 
- z 9→16: annulus Ø22→Ø50 (top pocket, open at top face) — at z=9, the layer starts over the web: the pocket void from z=9→16 is fine (it's a hole going up, each layer is an annulus on the previous annulus). At z=9 the inner boundary jumps from Ø12.4 back to Ø22 — the new layer's inner wall Ø22 is printed over the web's hole edge... the layer at z=9 is an annulus Ø22→Ø50 sitting on the web (solid from Ø12.4→Ø50 below) — fully supported ✓.

So the problem zone is exactly the web layer transition: a 4.8mm wide annular overhang (from Ø22 wall inward to Ø12.4 hole). This printed badly on the coupon ("loose loops and tangles around the hole; hole partly closed").

Fixes:
A) Reorient the wheel print: print standing? A Ø50×16 wheel on its edge: the pockets become horizontal voids with roofs — worse bridging (7mm tall pockets with flat roofs = bridging 22mm... the pocket roof spans the full 22mm circle → bad).

B) Split the wheel into two halves, each printed pocket-side-up? If a half-wheel is printed with its pocket opening UP (facing away from bed), the pocket walls print as a tube standing... let me think: half-wheel = 8mm thick disc with a 7mm-deep pocket from the top face: printing pocket-up: layers from bottom: solid disc layers 0→1 (the 1mm face ring... wait the half is 8 thick: pocket 7 deep from top leaves 1mm floor). Pocket opening up means: the void is carved from the top: as printed bottom-up: layers z 0→1: solid disc Ø50; layers z 1→8: annulus Ø22→Ø50. Every layer is an annulus on a solid base — NO overhangs at all! The pocket is a "well" that opens upward — completely print-friendly. Then the two halves are glued or bolted together? Hmm, gluing halves is meh but common. But we don't need to split! 

C) Just reorient the FULL wheel: print with the web hole... the problem is the inward overhang at the web. If the wheel prints with pockets opening upward on BOTH sides — impossible for one solid piece (both pockets open up = they'd meet at the web; the web floor of the upper pocket is the ceiling of the lower pocket... the lower pocket's "ceiling" (web underside) overhangs when pocket opens up? Let me think: lower pocket opens DOWNWARD in my current orientation (bed side) — that's fine (it's a well going down... no wait, if it opens downward at the bed, the bed face is the pocket mouth — the pocket is a recess in the bottom face: printing: layers 0→7 are annulus (void inside Ø22 from the very first layer) — supported, fine). Upper pocket opens UP at z=16 — as a well opening upward: layers 9→16 annulus on the web below: the web at z=7→9 is solid under the Ø22→Ø50 annulus — fine, no overhang there. The ONLY overhang is the web layer itself: the web (Ø12.4→Ø50 disc) at z=7→9: its inner ring Ø12.4→Ø22 overhangs the bottom pocket void. 

So the fix for the wheel: eliminate that overhang. Options:

B1) Make the web hole much larger — no; the hole must be < spacer... actually the web hole just needs to clear the spacer Ø11.6 and let the clamp float. What if the web hole is SMALLER (Ø9) and the web IS clamped?? No — we established the web must not be clamped.

B2) Print the wheel with one pocket opening DOWN (at bed) and... the web overhang is unavoidable in a single-piece wheel printed flat, UNLESS we redesign the web as a cone/funnel: make the web hole transition with a 45° chamfer so the overhang becomes printable: i.e., the web's underside is conical from Ø22 (pocket wall) tapering up to Ø12.4 over the 2mm height: a 45° supported slope — no overhang! The web becomes a conical funnel: from the bottom pocket's Ø22 ceiling, sloping up at 45° to the Ø12.4 hole top. Slope support: at 45°, each layer's ring edge is supported by the layer below (the standard printable overhang angle). The cone: bottom edge Ø22 at z=7, top edge Ø12.4 at z=9 — radial change 4.8mm over 2mm height = slope angle atan(2/4.8) ≈ 22.6° from horizontal — that's a SHALLOW overhang (worse than 45°!). Hmm: to be printable, the surface must rise steeply: from Ø22 at z=7 to Ø12.4 at z=z_top: the height needed for 45° = 4.8mm → web would be 4.8 thick → wheel 7+4.8+7 = 18.8 thick — too thick (old is 16). Alternatively make the pocket depth smaller to give the cone room: pockets 6 deep each, web 4: cone from Ø22 at z=6 to Ø12.4 at z=10: 4mm rise for 4.8 radial = 39.9° from horizontal ≈ 50° from vertical — printable-ish (most printers handle 45°+ from horizontal... wait overhang angle convention: surface angle from horizontal: 45° is the usual limit; 40° from horizontal is marginal). Hmm. And making pockets 6 deep means bearings stick out 1mm beyond each face — actually that's FINE and even good (race faces 1mm proud of wheel faces → washers bear race faces directly, no pocket-mouth nesting; wheel faces 1mm recessed... the wheel face would be at race-1mm: the race proud 1mm acts as a spacer standoff; wheel width still 16 total: 6+4+6=16 ✓. Race faces proud by 1mm each side: the wheel's rolling contact unaffected. Clamp washers bear race faces ✓. The wheel is axially located by press fits still ✓.

But wait — the shallow cone also weakens the web and the cone is a big overhang area even at 40°... it's supported-slope printing (like a chamfer), totally standard. 40° from horizontal is borderline-ok; 45° is standard-safe. With pockets 5.5 deep and web 5: radial 4.8 over 5mm rise = 46° from horizontal ✓ safe. Then bearings (7 wide) protrude 1.5mm beyond each face. Race faces proud 1.5mm. Wheel 16 = 5.5+5+5.5 ✓. Hmm, bearings sticking out 1.5mm each side — the washer (1.6 thick) bears the race face which is 1.5mm proud of the wheel face: the stack gains 3mm vs flush — bolt length: recompute: 3 washers 4.8 + t + 14 + 2.05 + 8 = t+28.85 same as before (the geometry along the bolt is identical — race faces are the reference planes regardless of proud/recessed!). ✓ No change to bolt math. 

And the cone: from pocket wall Ø22 at the pocket bottom... wait, the cone must be INSIDE the web: the web spans z 5.5→10.5 (5mm thick); the bottom pocket void: Ø22 from z=0→5.5; at z=5.5 the ceiling of the bottom pocket: instead of a flat ceiling with a Ø12.4 hole, the ceiling slopes from Ø22 at z=5.5 up... no wait — the cone slopes INWARD as z increases: at z=5.5 the void boundary is Ø22 (continuing the pocket wall); going up, the void narrows: at z=10.5 the void is Ø12.4 (the hole). The material is OUTSIDE the void: the web material fills from Ø_void(z) out to Ø50?? No — the web hole is only Ø12.4 at the top; the void at z=7 is Ø~17.2... the void between the pockets is a cone-frustum-shaped hole: wide at the bottom pocket (Ø22) narrowing to Ø12.4 at the top pocket. So the "web" is a disc Ø50 with a frustum hole. When printing bottom-up: at z=5.5, layer boundary: the annulus layer at z=5.5→5.7 has inner edge at Ø21.6 (narrowing): the new inner edge is printed over... the layer below at z<5.5 had void Ø22: the new layer's material extends inward from Ø21.6 to Ø34... the ring Ø12.4-ish... hmm wait I need to be careful: the overhang is where new material extends beyond the footprint of the void below? The void below (pocket) is Ø22; the new layer's void is Ø21.6: the new layer ADDS material in the ring Ø21.6→Ø22 over the void — that's a 0.2mm inward step per 0.2mm layer = 45° ✓ supported (each layer steps in 0.2 while rising 0.2 — 45° overhang, standard printable). So a 45° cone: void narrows 0.2mm per layer. From Ø22 to Ø12.4 = 4.8mm radial = 24 layers = 4.8mm height. So web thickness 4.8 → wheel = 7 + 4.8 + 7 = 18.8. To keep 16 total with bearings flush... we can't have both flush faces AND printable cone. With pockets 5.5 + web 5.0: cone rise available 5.0 ≥ 4.8 ✓ 45.6° — just enough! So: pockets 5.5 deep (bearings protrude 1.5mm per side), web 5.0 with 45° conical funnel from Ø22 down... wait direction: bottom pocket void Ø22 at z 0→5.5; cone from z=5.5 (Ø22) narrowing to z=10.5 (Ø12.4): rise 5.0, radial 4.8 → angle from horizontal = atan(5.0/4.8) = 46.2° ✓ printable. Top pocket void: Ø22 from z=10.5→16, opening at top ✓ no overhang.

Check the web at its thinnest: at the top of the cone, the material between Ø12.4 hole and... the web is solid Ø50 minus the frustum void — plenty strong. The clamp: spacer Ø11.6 passes through the Ø12.4 hole ✓ with 0.4 clearance. The washers bear race faces (proud 1.5mm) ✓ never touch the cone or wheel faces (washer Ø16 vs race face region ✓).

Hmm wait, one more check: the bottom pocket printed as annulus z 0→5.5 with void Ø22 open at bed — fine. At z=5.5 the cone starts narrowing: fine as computed. But ALSO: the transition at z=10.5 from cone (void Ø12.4) to top pocket (void Ø22): the layer at z=10.5 jumps the void from Ø12.4 to Ø22: the new layer is an annulus Ø22→Ø50 printed ON the web below (solid Ø12.4→Ø50 at z<10.5): the annulus' inner region Ø12.4→Ø22... wait the new layer at z=10.5 is annulus between Ø22 and Ø50 — all of it sits on material below? Below at z 10.3: material from Ø12.4(void smaller)→Ø50: yes material everywhere from Ø12.4 out: the annulus Ø22→Ø50 is fully supported ✓. 

So the printable wheel: pockets 5.5, web 5.0 with 45° cone. Bearings protrude 1.5mm each side. 

BUT WAIT — there's an even simpler classic solution: print the wheel in TWO HALVES and bolt them?? No — overcomplicates. Or: accept the bearing protrusion and skip the cone by making the web hole equal to the pocket diameter?? I.e., NO web at all: two separate bearing "washers"... no, single piece needed.

Alternative simplest fix: flip the print orientation: print the wheel with the OUTBOARD pocket facing DOWN?? Symmetric — same problem mirrored.

Alternative: make the web hole Ø22 = pocket diameter (no overhang at all — the "web" becomes a 2mm ring between... no wait: if web hole = Ø22 = pocket Ø, then the middle 2mm layer is an annulus Ø22→Ø50 — same annulus as pockets — NO step at all: the whole wheel becomes a TUBE: Ø50 outer, Ø22 inner, 16 tall, with... that's just a tube — the bearings would sit in a continuous Ø22 bore: two bearings back to back in one 14mm bore + 1mm face rings... wait wheel 16 with a through-bore Ø22×16: bearings inserted from each end: they can slide anywhere along the bore — axial position set by... the clamp: washers bear race faces; tighten: the bearings get pushed to the bore ends?? The bearing outer race Ø22 in bore Ø22: the bearing can slide axially freely; clamp washers (Ø16 < 22) bear the inner races: tightening pushes races toward each other... the races would slide inward, bearings end up somewhere in the middle, wheel loose axially (can slide 2mm total)... Actually: wheel slides axially relative to races?? The outer races are slip-fit in the bore; the wheel can slide along the bolt until... the wheel's face hits the washer? The washer Ø16 is INSIDE the bore Ø22: it can pass through! The whole clamp stack (washers Ø16) passes through the Ø22 bore: the wheel is axially unconstrained (it can slide 16mm along the bolt until the... nothing stops it except the nut/head outside the bore?? The head Ø13 > 22? No 13 < 22 — head also passes through! The wheel would slide OFF the bolt entirely!! Unless washers bigger than the bore. So: make the through-bore design with larger clamp flanges: printed clamp washers Ø26 (larger than bore 22) that sit ON the wheel faces (not inside)... then the clamp grips the WHEEL → wheel can't spin. No good.

So the cone-funnel design (B2) is the right fix for a single-piece wheel. Let me also reconsider the coupon failure #1: "21.99 mm seat: won't go in": pocket measured 21.99 yet bearing won't enter?? If the pocket is truly 21.99 round and smooth, a 22.0 bearing is line-to-line — should slide with thumb force. "Won't go in" suggests the pocket is effectively undersized locally (polygonal: measured across flats 21.99 maybe, but corners... a printed circular hole is a polygon of ~perimeter segments; the measured "21.99" might be across flats while vertices are larger... vertices make it BIGGER not smaller. Undersized local: if they measured with caliper jaws at one diameter and got 21.99 but the hole is out-of-round with a smaller dimension elsewhere, or there's a bulge/seam. Also the drooping roof loops could intrude into the pocket mouth region?? The droop was at the top (roof) — z 7→9 — the pocket mouth is at z=0 (bed) — droop at top wouldn't block insertion from the bottom... The bearing inserted from the pocket mouth (z=0): travels to z=7 ceiling: if the drooping roof sagged DOWN into the pocket (sag hangs down into the void), the ceiling is effectively lower than 7 and lumpy — bearing 7 wide hits the sagged roof → "won't go in" fully!! That explains it: the failed roof drooped into the pocket, so the bearing can't seat. So failure #2 (bad roof) likely CAUSED failure #1. 

So the main fix: eliminate the overhang roof. The cone design does that for the wheel. 

Now what about the coupon — redesign it to test the NEW geometry: a coupon that mimics one pocket + cone? A coupon half: disc Ø34, height 8 (mimicking wheel half: 5.5 pocket + 2.5 of cone?): pocket from bed z 0→5.5 (void Ø22 open at bed), then cone z 5.5→8 narrowing 22→14.6 (2.5 rise, 3.7 radial → 34° — NOT printable... coupon cone must also be ≥45°: radial 4.8 needs 4.8 rise: coupon 5.5+4.8=10.3 tall. Fine: coupon Ø34 × 10.3: pocket 5.5 + cone to Ø12.4 at top... then also test the top face?? The coupon tests: (a) pocket press fit at the bed face, (b) the cone prints cleanly, (c) bearing seats with race face proud 1.5mm... wait in the new wheel the pocket is 5.5 deep and bearing protrudes 1.5 beyond the pocket... in the coupon the pocket is 5.5 deep from the bed face: bearing inserted from bed side sits 1.5mm proud of the bed plane — flush test differs but fine.

Hmm, but actually — hold on. Let me reconsider the whole design. Is there a simpler, more robust wheel architecture given the print constraints? 

Classic approach used by many printed roller designs: wheel with a THROUGH-bore where the bearings are retained by the clamp stack acting on the wheel faces with shoulders: e.g., wheel bore Ø22 (bearings slip in), and printed internal shoulders?? 

Alternative classic: two bearing pockets each open at a face, each with a retention lip — we dropped lips due to the rigid-surround problem, but actually a lip CAN work as a snap if the lip is a cantilever ring with relief: e.g., 3-4 interrupted lip segments (snap fingers) that flex inward... at Ø22, segments flex fine. But that adds complexity; and the coupon roof problem would become lip overhang problems (lips overhang too — same bridging issue on the underside of lips! The lip protruding into the pocket from the ceiling = overhang ring — same failure). Unless lips are printed as part of the pocket WALL slope... no.

The cone design avoids ALL overhangs. I like it. Let me also double check the cone doesn't interfere with bearing insertion: bearing inserted into the bottom pocket from the bed-side face: pocket Ø22 depth 5.5: bearing slides in, sits at bottom... wait the pocket bottom is the BED face (z=0) — the bearing rests against z=0 plane?? The pocket is cut from z=0 to z=5.5: the bearing sits with its outer face at z=0 (flush with wheel face) and inner face at z=7 — protruding 1.5mm INTO the cone region (cone void at z=7 is Ø22-2*(7-5.5)=Ø19... wait cone void diameter at z: Ø_v(z) = 22 - 2*(z-5.5)*(4.8/5.0)... at z=7: 22 - 2*1.5*0.96 = 19.12. The bearing occupies Ø22 up to z=7: but the void at z=5.5→7 narrows from 22 to 19.12: the bearing (Ø22 rigid) can't be at z>5.5!! The bearing is 7 wide: pocket only 5.5 deep → the bearing MUST extend 1.5mm into the cone zone where the void is < 22 → INTERFERENCE. The bearing would be stopped at the cone and sit proud... let me recompute: bearing inserted from z=0 face: it can slide until its outer race hits the cone: the cone at the bearing's leading face (z = bearing position + 7): bearing leading face reaches z where void ≥ 22 → only z ≤ 5.5. So the bearing rests with leading face at z=5.5 → occupies z -1.5?? Negative — impossible: the bearing would protrude 1.5mm BEYOND the z=0 face (proud of the wheel face) ✓ that's exactly what I said: race faces proud 1.5mm. The bearing bottom face at z=-1.5 relative... in printed coordinates the bearing face sits 1.5mm below the wheel's z=0 face plane — i.e., proud of the face. ✓ Fine.

But hmm — wait, now the "face ring" is 0 at the pocket mouth... the wheel face at z=0 is an annulus Ø22→Ø50 (0.0mm thick ring before the pocket starts). The bearing protrudes 1.5: the wheel face plane and the race face plane are 1.5 apart. The WASHER (Ø16, on the race face) — the washer is 1.6 thick: it sits 1.5 proud, spanning z -1.6→0.1... the washer edge at Ø16 vs wheel face annulus starts at Ø22: no contact ✓. OK.

But now think about the OUTBOARD side: symmetric: pocket 5.5 from z=16 face, cone from z=10.5... wait the cone: bottom pocket cone z 5.5→10.5 narrowing upward; top pocket: void Ø22 z 10.5→16; between the two cones?? Hold on — I only have ONE web (2mm→ now 5mm) between the two pockets. The cone is the transition on ONE side?? Let me redo the geometry: wheel z 0→16. Bottom pocket: void Ø22, z 0→5.5. Top pocket: void Ø22, z 10.5→16. Web: z 5.5→10.5, with the hole. The hole must clear the spacer Ø11.6 → ≥ Ø12.4 somewhere. The web's hole shape: I want NO overhang when printing bottom-up. Overhang occurs where material extends over void. Going up from z=5.5: below is void Ø22 (pocket). The web hole at z=5.5+ε: if the hole is Ø12.4 at z=5.5 (flat web with small hole), material ring Ø12.4→Ø22 at z 5.5+ overhangs → bad. If the hole at z=5.5 is Ø22 and narrows going up to Ø12.4 at z=10.5 → cone → printable ✓. At z=10.5 the hole is Ø12.4; above that, the top pocket void jumps to Ø22 — supported ✓ (new material above is supported by the web below... the top pocket annulus at z=10.5 sits on the web which is solid from Ø12.4 outward ✓).

So the single cone spans the whole web 5.0 tall ✓ as I designed. The cone void at z=10.5 is Ø12.4 = hole ✓. The spacer Ø11.6 passes through the narrowest point Ø12.4 ✓ 0.4 clearance. But wait — the clamp: washers bear race faces at z=-1.5 (below z=0, proud) and z=17.5 (above 16, proud)?? No wait: top pocket: void Ø22 from z=10.5→16, open at top face z=16. Bearing inserted from top: slides down until leading face hits the cone top: cone at z=10.5 has void Ø12.4 < 22 → bearing leading face stops at z=10.5: bearing occupies z 10.5→17.5: protrudes 1.5 above z=16 ✓. Race face (inner) at z=17.5?? The bearing's INNER race face is on the... which side of the bearing faces out? The bearing is symmetric — inner race faces are both on the flat faces of the bearing. The clamp washer on the outboard side bears the bearing's outboard flat face at z=17.5 (proud 1.5). The clamp chain: head-side washer at z=-1.6 (bearing race face at z=-1.5... washer 1.6 thick: z -3.1→-1.5) — washer bears race face at z=-1.5 ✓; other washer at z 17.5→19.1 bears race face at 17.5 ✓. Between them: races (z -1.5→5.5 and 10.5→17.5) and spacer spanning z 5.5→10.5 = 5.0!! The spacer must now be 5.0 long, not 2.05!! Wait: the gap between the inner races: race A spans z -1.5→5.5 (7 wide), race B spans 10.5→17.5: gap between them = 10.5-5.5 = 5.0. The spacer: Ø11.6 tube 5.0 long — BUT the cone void at its narrowest is Ø12.4 — the spacer Ø11.6 × 5.0 long fits inside the cone void: at z=5.5 void is 22, narrowing to 12.4 at 10.5: spacer Ø11.6 fits everywhere (11.6 < 12.4) ✓. The spacer is clamped between the race faces ✓. And the web material: the cone void around the spacer: min 12.4 vs spacer 11.6: 0.4 radial gap — the spacer must not rub: it's centered by the races ✓.

Hmm wait, but now the CONE is a large surface... and the web is 5mm thick — the wheel is fine. But now check: does the CONE void interfere with the bearing's outer race sides? The bearing sits in the pocket (Ø22 region z 0→5.5): the race corner at z=5.5... bearing corner chamfers fine.

Wait, actually now reconsider whether bearings protruding 1.5mm each side is a problem for the track: the wheel width is still 16 (tread band z 0→16 at Ø50) — the bearings are inside Ø22, nowhere near the tread ✓. The protruding race faces + washers stick out axially: total assembly width = 16 + 2*(1.5 + washer 1.6) = 16+6.2 = 22.2?? vs old wheel 16 in a channel: the old assembly's width across its widest point — the old axle/nut also stuck out. The washers Ø16 sit in the pocket-mouth region — they're within the wheel's Ø50 envelope axially protruding 3.1mm each side. If the channel is only slightly wider than 16... the washers would foul the channel walls!! Hmm. In the ORIGINAL design (flush races, pockets 7 deep), the washers sat inside the pocket mouths (within the 16 width) — total width 16 + locknut protrusion only. In the new cone design, washers protrude 3.1mm each side → assembly width 22.2. That could foul tight channels!

Hmm. Trade-off. Can I keep races flush AND printable? Options:

C) Two-piece wheel: print TWO half-wheels, each pocket-up (zero overhang), then join. Joining methods: glue (CA/epoxy — glue isn't in the hardware list... "use only the hardware listed" — glue as adhesive consumable: risky per rules), or MECHANICAL: the two halves bolted together around the perimeter with... M3 screws through the rim? That changes hardware and adds failure modes; also the seam runs through the tread — bad for a rolling surface.

D) Keep single piece, pockets 7 deep flush, but fix the web overhang differently: make the web hole SMALLER than the pocket and accept a SHORT overhang with support: the overhang ring width = (22 - hole)/2. If the web hole is Ø12.4 → 4.8mm annular bridge — failed. If the web hole is Ø20 → 1mm annular overhang — prints fine typically (1mm overhang bridging is usually OK-ish). But hole Ø20 > spacer 11.6 — the spacer no longer needed!! Wait: if the web hole is Ø20, the clamp can't bear on... the clamp washers are Ø16 < 20: they pass through the web hole and bear the race faces ✓ (that was always the case). The web hole just needs to NOT be clamped: with hole Ø20 > washer Ø16: the washers float inside the hole, bearing only the races ✓✓. So why did I need the spacer at all? The spacer spanned the 2mm gap between race faces so the clamp (head-washer...washer-nut) could compress the races WITHOUT squeezing the web. With hole Ø20, the clamp passes THROUGH the web hole: head washer...wait the clamp stack: head — washer — [bracket] — washer — raceA — [?? gap 2mm between raceA and raceB] — raceB — washer — locknut. The 2mm gap between the races still needs something to span it, or the clamp just... the nut tightens: it pulls raceB toward raceA; the 2mm gap closes only if something fills it or the races move — they're held by pockets. The washer under the locknut is at the outboard face; the gap is INTERNAL. So yes, still need the spacer (or make the races touch by pocket depth 8 with 1mm recess — rejected earlier due to washer reach... wait now reconsider: pockets 8 deep, race faces recessed 1mm below wheel faces: clamp washer Ø16 sits in the pocket mouth: does it reach the race face 1mm down? The washer is flat 1.6 thick: it would rest on the pocket mouth rim (wheel face annulus at Ø16<22?? the pocket mouth rim is at Ø22: the washer Ø16 is INSIDE the mouth — it drops down and rests ON the race face 1mm below the face plane ✓!!   - Clamp: bolt head — washer — [bracket] — washer — race A face — bearing A — (1.5 gap, no spacer) — bearing B — race B face — washer — lock nut.
